Definition: from G2749; a hamlet (as if laid down):--town, village.
KeyPassages: Matthew 9:35; Matthew 10:11; Mark 6:6; Luke 5:17; John 7:42; Acts 8:25
BiblicalUsage: Kome is a village, a hamlet. Matthew 9:35 has Jesus going about all the cities and villages, teaching and preaching and healing, Matthew 10:11 tells the disciples to enquire who is worthy in whatever town they enter, Mark 6:6 has Jesus going round about the villages, teaching, Luke 5:17 has Pharisees come out of every town of Galilee and Judaea, John 7:42 says Christ cometh out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was, and Acts 8:25 has the apostles preaching the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the villages are where the gospel did its ordinary work: not only in Jerusalem, but in every town of Galilee and in the villages of the Samaritans. I hold that Bethlehem the village is the centre of the word, because Christ came out of it, and the villages He walked are the measure of His ministry.
